key_insight: PG-KINN pairs a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network trial function with an independent Petrov-Galerkin test space to solve PDEs more accurately and robustly than strong-form or energy-form physics-informed models.
engineering_relevance: This gives computational mechanics and inverse-design workflows a more stable physics-informed solver for nonlinear, non-self-adjoint, and parameter-identification PDE problems.
method: KAN as the trial space with learnable spline activations
Compactly supported piecewise-polynomial test functions in a Petrov-Galerkin weak form
Gauss-Legendre quadrature after integration by parts to reduce derivative order
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains on benchmarks including crack singularities, stress concentration, Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, inverse heterogeneous-media identification, and complex geometries versus MLP and prior KAN baselines.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful choice of test-space resolution and quadrature, so implementation details may strongly affect stability and accuracy.
paper_title: PG-KINN: A Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs
